claim: Mecp2-deficient mice show fear regulation impairment.
source: Mecp2-deficient mice show fear regulation impairment; however, the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying this abnormal behavior are largely uncharacterized.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established finding that motivates the current study.

claim: Mecp2 gene deficiency in cholinergic interneurons of the nucleus accumbens dramatically impaired fear learning.
source: Here, we showed that Mecp2 gene deficiency in cholinergic interneurons of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) dramatically impaired fear learning.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral data in Figure 1.

claim: Spontaneous activity of cholinergic interneurons in Mecp2-deficient mice decreased.
source: We further found that spontaneous activity of cholinergic interneurons in Mecp2-deficient mice decreased, mediated by enhanced inhibitory transmission via α2-containing GABAA receptors.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiological recordings in Figure 3.

claim: Decreased spontaneous activity of cholinergic interneurons in Mecp2-deficient mice is mediated by enhanced inhibitory transmission via α2-containing GABAA receptors.
source: We further found that spontaneous activity of cholinergic interneurons in Mecp2-deficient mice decreased, mediated by enhanced inhibitory transmission via α2-containing GABAA receptors.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3 showing increased α2-GABAA receptor expression and mIPSC amplitude.

claim: Impaired fear retrieval in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was rescued with MeCP2 restoration in ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc.
source: With MeCP2 restoration, opto- and chemo-genetic activation, and RNA interference in ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc, impaired fear retrieval was rescued.
evidence: This rescue effect is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2.

claim: Impaired fear retrieval in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was rescued with optogenetic activation of ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc.
source: With MeCP2 restoration, opto- and chemo-genetic activation, and RNA interference in ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc, impaired fear retrieval was rescued.
evidence: This rescue effect is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: Impaired fear retrieval in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was rescued with chemogenetic activation of ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc.
source: With MeCP2 restoration, opto- and chemo-genetic activation, and RNA interference in ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc, impaired fear retrieval was rescued.
evidence: This rescue effect is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: Impaired fear retrieval in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was rescued with RNA interference targeting α2-GABAA receptors in ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc.
source: With MeCP2 restoration, opto- and chemo-genetic activation, and RNA interference in ChAT-expressing interneurons of the NAc, impaired fear retrieval was rescued.
evidence: This rescue effect is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: MeCP2 is a nuclear protein involved in the transcriptional repression of target genes.
source: MeCP2 is a nuclear protein involved in the transcriptional repression of target genes (Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007; Lyst and Bird, 2015; Qiu, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mice lacking Mecp2 can reproduce various Rett syndrome (RTT) phenotypes, including motor dysfunction, anxiety behavior, abnormal social behavior as well as impaired learning and memory.
source: Mice lacking Mecp2 can reproduce various Rett syndrome (RTT) phenotypes, including motor dysfunction, anxiety behavior, abnormal social behavior as well as impaired learning and memory (Shahbazian et al., 2002; Gemelli et al., 2006; Adachi et al., 2009; Ito-Ishida et al., 2015; Chao et al., 2010; Fyffe et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2001; Guy et al., 2001; Moretti et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Cholinergic neurons play an important role in learning and memory.
source: Given the important role of cholinergic neurons in learning and memory (Jiang et al., 2016; Brown et al., 2012; Picciotto et al., 2012; Letzkus et al., 2011; Likhtik and Johansen, 2019; Hasselmo, 2006; Yu and Dayan, 2005; Aitta-Aho et al., 2018), we proposed that conditional deletion of Mecp2 from cholinergic neurons may result in fear encoding dysfunction.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: There are two primary sources of acetylcholine in the brain: projection neurons located in the pedunculopontine, medial habenula, and basal forebrain, and local interneurons located in the striatum and NAc.
source: There are two primary sources of acetylcholine in the brain, that is, projection neurons located in the pedunculopontine, medial habenula, and basal forebrain (BF), and local interneurons located in the striatum and NAc (Aitta-Aho et al., 2018; Floresco, 2015; Kreitzer, 2009; Ren et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cholinergic projection neurons of the BF may contribute to impaired social interaction, decreased anxiety- and depression-like behaviors as well as elevated epilepsy susceptibility in Mecp2-deficient mice, with no effect on hippocampus-dependent learning and memory.
source: Our previous study suggested that cholinergic projection neurons of the BF may contribute to impaired social interaction, decreased anxiety- and depression-like behaviors as well as elevated epilepsy susceptibility in Mecp2-deficient mice, with no effect on hippocampus-dependent learning and memory (Zhang et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: MeCP2 is highly expressed in NAc neurons.
source: Although MeCP2 is highly expressed in NAc neurons (Deng et al., 2010), relatively little is known about how MeCP2 regulates NAc cholinergic interneuron function.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Acetylcholine signaling is directly required for the modulation of local circuit activity and associative learning.
source: Despite the paucity of cholinergic interneurons in the NAc, acetylcholine signaling is directly required for the modulation of local circuit activity and associative learning (Cardinal et al., 2002; Luchicchi et al., 2014; Mamaligas and Ford, 2016; Picciotto et al., 2012; Shen et al., 2005; Witten et al., 2010; Brown et al., 2012; Hikida et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Clinical research has implicated the NAc as one of the affected brain regions in RTT patients.
source: Additionally, clinical research has implicated the NAc as one of the affected brain regions in RTT patients (Reiss et al., 1993; Subramaniam et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice were generated by crossing ChatCre mice with mice carrying the loxp-flanked allele (Mecp2flox/-).
source: We first deleted Mecp2 specifically from cholinergic neurons by crossing ChatCre mice with mice carrying the loxp-flanked allele (Mecp2flox/-), hereafter referred to as Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
evidence: This describes the method used to generate the conditional knockout mice.

claim: There was a remarkable reduction in the expression of MeCP2 in the cholinergic neurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: Fluorescent immunohistochemistry results demonstrated a remarkable reduction in the expression of MeCP2 in the cholinergic neurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice (Figure 1A–E), thus confirming the efficiency of Mecp2 deletion.
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1A-E.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice displayed increased freezing across trials in the training day.
source: The Chat-Mecp2-/y mice displayed increased freezing across trials in the training day (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is shown in the fear conditioning data in Figure 1F.

claim: Freezing time of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was significantly decreased on the last trial compared to control groups, suggesting an impairment in fear learning.
source: However, compared to the other three control groups, freezing time of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was significantly decreased on the last trial, suggesting an impairment in fear learning (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice showed decreased freezing time in the context retrieval test.
source: In the context and tone retrieval test, Chat-Mecp2-/y mice also showed decreased freezing time (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice showed decreased freezing time in the tone retrieval test.
source: In the context and tone retrieval test, Chat-Mecp2-/y mice also showed decreased freezing time (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The difference in retrieval test with Chat-Mecp2-/y mice disappeared after normalizing to the last trial in the training day, further supporting the fear learning deficits.
source: The difference in retrieval test with Chat-Mecp2-/y mice disappeared after normalizing to the last trial in the training day, further supporting the fear learning deficits (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice exhibited normal ability in pain detection.
source: The Chat-Mecp2-/y mice exhibited normal ability in pain detection (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice demonstrated normal locomotor activity without significant differences in immobility time in the open field tests.
source: The Chat-Mecp2-/y mice demonstrated normal locomotor activity without significant differences in immobility time in the open field tests (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice showed no deficit in the Y maze test, suggesting normal working memory ability.
source: Furthermore, these mice showed no deficit in the Y maze (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) or Morris water maze tests (Zhang et al., 2016b), suggesting normal working and spatial memory ability.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G and cited from previous work.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice showed no deficit in Morris water maze tests, suggesting normal spatial memory ability.
source: Furthermore, these mice showed no deficit in the Y maze (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) or Morris water maze tests (Zhang et al., 2016b), suggesting normal working and spatial memory ability.
evidence: This is cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: Approximately 73% of ChAT positive neurons were infected by the AAV virus in the NAc.
source: We employed immunohistochemistry to confirm the recombination efficiency of the AAV/Mecp2 virus (Figure 2A) and revealed that ~73% of ChAT positive neurons were infected by the AAV virus and over 85% of GFP-labeled neurons were stained positively for MeCP2 in the NAc (Figure 2B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Over 85% of GFP-labeled neurons were stained positively for MeCP2 in the NAc.
source: We employed immunohistochemistry to confirm the recombination efficiency of the AAV/Mecp2 virus (Figure 2A) and revealed that ~73% of ChAT positive neurons were infected by the AAV virus and over 85% of GFP-labeled neurons were stained positively for MeCP2 in the NAc (Figure 2B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Fear learning deficit of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was rescued towards the end of training with MeCP2 restoration in the cholinergic neurons of NAc, but not medial septum.
source: It appeared that fear learning deficit of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice was rescued towards the end of training with MeCP2 restoration in the cholinergic neurons of NAc, but not medial septum (MS) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice injected with the AAV/Mecp2 virus in NAc showed a significant enhancement in context fear retrieval tests.
source: Consistently, in the context and tone fear retrieval tests, although the freezing level was not comparable to that of the AAV/GFP-injected ChatCre mice, Chat-Mecp2-/y mice injected with the AAV/Mecp2 virus showed a significant enhancement (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Chat-Mecp2-/y mice injected with the AAV/Mecp2 virus in NAc showed a significant enhancement in tone fear retrieval tests.
source: Consistently, in the context and tone fear retrieval tests, although the freezing level was not comparable to that of the AAV/GFP-injected ChatCre mice, Chat-Mecp2-/y mice injected with the AAV/Mecp2 virus showed a significant enhancement (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D.

claim: MeCP2 restoration in the cholinergic neurons of MS had no effect on fear regulation in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: In contrast, MeCP2 restoration in the cholinergic neurons of MS, which has been reported to mediate sensory induced aversion (Zhang et al., 2018), had no effect on fear regulation in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: The spontaneous spiking rate of NAc cholinergic interneurons was significantly decreased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in cell-attached configuration.
source: The spontaneous spiking rate of NAc cholinergic interneurons was significantly decreased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in both cell-attached (Figure 3A,B) and whole-cell configurations (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The spontaneous spiking rate of NAc cholinergic interneurons was significantly decreased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in whole-cell configuration.
source: The spontaneous spiking rate of NAc cholinergic interneurons was significantly decreased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in both cell-attached (Figure 3A,B) and whole-cell configurations (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: There was a significant increase in spontaneous firing rate in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice with MeCP2/AAV expression compared with GFP/AAV expression.
source: We also evaluated the spontaneous firing rate and found a significant increase in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice with MeCP2/AAV expression compared with GFP/AAV expression (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: NAc cholinergic interneurons are considered tonic firing neurons.
source: First, we measured the spontaneous firing frequency of cholinergic interneurons in brain slices, as NAc cholinergic interneurons are considered tonic firing neurons (Zahar and Morris, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: There were no significant differences in intrinsic properties of cholinergic interneurons in the NAc between Chat-Mecp2-/y and control mice.
source: Thus, we first measured the intrinsic properties of the cholinergic interneurons in the NAc and found no significant differences between Chat-Mecp2-/y and control mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The frequency of mIPSCs was not altered in the NAc cholinergic interneurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: Although the frequency of mIPSCs was not altered in the NAc cholinergic interneurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice, their amplitude was significantly increased compared to that in control mice, indicating abnormal changes in postsynaptic connections in the cholinergic interneurons (Figure 3G,H; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The amplitude of mIPSCs was significantly increased in the NAc cholinergic interneurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice compared to control mice.
source: Although the frequency of mIPSCs was not altered in the NAc cholinergic interneurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice, their amplitude was significantly increased compared to that in control mice, indicating abnormal changes in postsynaptic connections in the cholinergic interneurons (Figure 3G,H; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: Miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) were rarely recorded in the cholinergic interneurons (mEPSC frequency <0.1 Hz).
source: Consistent with previous studies (Bennett and Wilson, 1999), our whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings showed that miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) were rarely recorded in the cholinergic interneurons (mEPSC frequency <0.1 Hz, data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the text and consistent with cited literature.

claim: The GABAA receptor is a heteropentameric ligand-gated chloride channel that mediates major inhibitory transmission in the brain.
source: The GABAA receptor is a heteropentameric ligand-gated chloride channel that mediates major inhibitory transmission in the brain (Farrant and Nusser, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Receptors with different subunits are distributed in different neurons and play distinct roles in current responses.
source: Receptors with different subunits are distributed in different neurons and play distinct roles in current responses (Lavoie et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Approximately 70% of ChAT-positive neurons expressed detectable levels of α2 subunits in the NAc.
source: Surprisingly, we found that approximately 70% of ChAT-positive neurons expressed detectable levels of α2 subunits in the NAc (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3I.

claim: There was little expression of α1 subunits in the NAc cholinergic interneurons.
source: In contrast, there was little expression of α1 subunits in the NAc cholinergic interneurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: α2 GABAA receptor expression was increased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: We found that α2 was increased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice but α1 was unchanged (Figure 3J; Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3J by western blot analysis.

claim: α1 GABAA receptor expression was unchanged in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: We found that α2 was increased in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice but α1 was unchanged (Figure 3J; Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C by western blot analysis.

claim: Immunohistochemistry results showed a significant increase in α2 expression specifically in the cholinergic interneurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice compared to those of ChatCre mice.
source: Furthermore, immunohistochemistry results showed a significant increase in α2 expression specifically in the cholinergic interneurons of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice compared to those of ChatCre mice (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Potentiating the α2-GABAA receptors with L-838,417 (2 μM) in bath solution significantly decreased the firing frequency of cholinergic interneurons in NAc slices from control mice.
source: Potentiating the α2-GABAA receptors with L-838,417 (2 μM) in bath solution significantly decreased the firing frequency of cholinergic interneurons in NAc slices from both control (Figure 3L,M) and Chat-Mecp2-/y mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3L,M.

claim: Potentiating the α2-GABAA receptors with L-838,417 (2 μM) in bath solution significantly decreased the firing frequency of cholinergic interneurons in NAc slices from Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: Potentiating the α2-GABAA receptors with L-838,417 (2 μM) in bath solution significantly decreased the firing frequency of cholinergic interneurons in NAc slices from both control (Figure 3L,M) and Chat-Mecp2-/y mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Both the frequency and amplitude of sIPSC have been increased after L-838,417 treatment.
source: Further, we also compared the effect of L-838,417 on GABAergic current and found that both the frequency and amplitude of sIPSC have been increased after treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F.

claim: 1 μM clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) activated spiking in hM3Dq-expressed NAc cholinergic interneurons.
source: Electrophysiological analysis of NAc slices confirmed that 1 μM clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) activated spiking in hM3Dq-expressed NAc cholinergic interneurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Activation of NAc cholinergic interneurons significantly increased the freezing level of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in the training process.
source: Activation of NAc cholinergic interneurons significantly increased the freezing level of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in the training process (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), as well as the context and tone fear memory retrieval process (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Activation of NAc cholinergic interneurons significantly increased the freezing level of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in the context fear memory retrieval process.
source: Activation of NAc cholinergic interneurons significantly increased the freezing level of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in the training process (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), as well as the context and tone fear memory retrieval process (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Activation of NAc cholinergic interneurons significantly increased the freezing level of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in the tone fear memory retrieval process.
source: Activation of NAc cholinergic interneurons significantly increased the freezing level of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice in the training process (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), as well as the context and tone fear memory retrieval process (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Electrophysiological recordings of NAc cholinergic interneurons reliably revealed one-to-one, photo-stimulation locked action potential firing at frequencies up to 10 Hz.
source: Electrophysiological recordings of NAc cholinergic interneurons reliably revealed one-to-one, photo-stimulation locked action potential firing at frequencies up to 10 Hz (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons (8 Hz) only during fear learning rescued fear deficits in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: We found that optogenetic activation of cholinergic interneurons (8 Hz) only during fear learning also rescued fear deficits in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice (Figure 4E,F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4E,F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Activation of NAc cholinergic neurons had no effect on freezing in the absence of shock delivery.
source: We also confirmed that activation of NAc cholinergic neurons had no effect on freezing in the absence of shock delivery (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H.

claim: Application of CNO before fear conditioning significantly decreased context fear responses during the retrieval process in ChatCre mice with AAV-DIO-hM4Di-mCherry delivered into the NAc.
source: Application of CNO before fear conditioning significantly decreased context and tone fear responses during the retrieval process (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Application of CNO before fear conditioning significantly decreased tone fear responses during the retrieval process in ChatCre mice with AAV-DIO-hM4Di-mCherry delivered into the NAc.
source: Application of CNO before fear conditioning significantly decreased context and tone fear responses during the retrieval process (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Inhibition of cholinergic neurons in NAc core impaired context fear.
source: Inhibition of cholinergic neurons in core or shell has similar effect on context/tone fear. However, if we only inhibit cholinergic neurons in NAc medial shell, only tone fear was impaired, with context fear intact, suggesting the heterogeneity within NAc shell (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Inhibition of cholinergic neurons in NAc core impaired tone fear.
source: Inhibition of cholinergic neurons in core or shell has similar effect on context/tone fear. However, if we only inhibit cholinergic neurons in NAc medial shell, only tone fear was impaired, with context fear intact, suggesting the heterogeneity within NAc shell (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Inhibition of cholinergic neurons in NAc medial shell impaired tone fear but not context fear.
source: Inhibition of cholinergic neurons in core or shell has similar effect on context/tone fear. However, if we only inhibit cholinergic neurons in NAc medial shell, only tone fear was impaired, with context fear intact, suggesting the heterogeneity within NAc shell (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: In the NAc of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice, neurons infected by AAV/α2RNAi showed significantly decreased mIPSC amplitude compared to the scrambled controls (AAV/sham).
source: In the NAc of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice, neurons infected by AAV/α2RNAi showed significantly decreased mIPSC amplitude compared to the scrambled controls (AAV/sham) (Figure 6B,C), but no changes in mIPSC frequency (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: In the NAc of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice, neurons infected by AAV/α2RNAi showed no changes in mIPSC frequency compared to the scrambled controls (AAV/sham).
source: In the NAc of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice, neurons infected by AAV/α2RNAi showed significantly decreased mIPSC amplitude compared to the scrambled controls (AAV/sham) (Figure 6B,C), but no changes in mIPSC frequency (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: AAV/α2RNAi showed specific infection in the cholinergic interneurons of the NAc and ~50% knockdown efficiency of α2-GABAA receptors in the cholinergic interneurons.
source: Immunohistochemical analysis also revealed AAV/α2RNAi specific infection in the cholinergic interneurons of the NAc and ~50% knockdown efficiency of α2-GABAA receptors in the cholinergic interneurons (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Down-regulating α2-GABAA receptors in the NAc of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice rescued the decreased spontaneous firing rates of NAc cholinergic interneurons.
source: Furthermore, we found that down-regulating α2-GABAA receptors in the NAc of Chat-Mecp2-/y mice rescued the decreased spontaneous firing rates of NAc cholinergic interneurons (Figure 5G,H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: The freezing response in the context fear retrieval period was markedly improved in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice infected with AAV/α2RNAi compared with the AAV/sham group.
source: Functionally, the freezing response in the context and tone fear retrieval period was markedly improved in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice infected with AAV/α2RNAi compared with the AAV/sham group (Figure 5I,J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The freezing response in the tone fear retrieval period was markedly improved in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice infected with AAV/α2RNAi compared with the AAV/sham group.
source: Functionally, the freezing response in the context and tone fear retrieval period was markedly improved in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice infected with AAV/α2RNAi compared with the AAV/sham group (Figure 5I,J).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Locomotor activity was not significantly changed in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice infected with AAV/α2RNAi, suggesting that the freezing behavior was not due to motor defects.
source: Locomotor activity was not significantly changed, suggesting that the freezing behavior was not due to motor defects (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5K.

claim: NpHR-mediated hyperpolarization efficiently blocked the spontaneous firing rates of cholinergic interneurons.
source: We verified functionality with slice recordings and found that NpHR-mediated hyperpolarization efficiently blocked the spontaneous firing rates of cholinergic interneurons (Figure 5G,H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: Inhibiting the spiking of cholinergic interneurons with yellow light (593 nm) only during the learning phase abolished the rescue effects of AAV/RNAi in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice.
source: Inhibiting the spiking of cholinergic interneurons with yellow light (593 nm) only during the learning phase abolished the rescue effects of AAV/RNAi in Chat-Mecp2-/y mice (Figure 5I,J) without affecting locomotion (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5I,J.

claim: Injection of L-838,417 into the bilateral NAc of wild-type mice 30 min prior to the training period of fear conditioning elicited significantly decreased freezing levels in context retrieval sessions.
source: In the retrieval sessions, identical scenery or tone elicited significantly decreased freezing levels in the L-838,417 group (Figure 6G,H), suggesting that activation of α2-containing GABAA receptors in the NAc was sufficient to dampen the spiking of cholinergic interneurons and impair fear behavior.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Injection of L-838,417 into the bilateral NAc of wild-type mice 30 min prior to the training period of fear conditioning elicited significantly decreased freezing levels in tone retrieval sessions.
source: In the retrieval sessions, identical scenery or tone elicited significantly decreased freezing levels in the L-838,417 group (Figure 6G,H), suggesting that activation of α2-containing GABAA receptors in the NAc was sufficient to dampen the spiking of cholinergic interneurons and impair fear behavior.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Activation of α2-containing GABAA receptors in the NAc was sufficient to dampen the spiking of cholinergic interneurons and impair fear behavior.
source: In the retrieval sessions, identical scenery or tone elicited significantly decreased freezing levels in the L-838,417 group (Figure 6G,H), suggesting that activation of α2-containing GABAA receptors in the NAc was sufficient to dampen the spiking of cholinergic interneurons and impair fear behavior.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral effects of L-838,417 shown in Figure 6G,H.

claim: Deficiency of MeCP2 in specific neuron types or regions results in RTT-like phenotypes in mice.
source: Deficiency of MeCP2 in specific neuron types or regions results in RTT-like phenotypes in mice (Fyffe et al., 2008; Guy et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PV-Mecp2-/y, CAMKII-Mecp2-/y, and MeCP2 region-specific deletion from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) results in anxiety-like behavior and impaired learning ability.
source: For example, PV-Mecp2-/y, CAMKII-Mecp2-/y, and MeCP2 region-specific deletion from the basolateral amygdala (BLA) results in anxiety-like behavior and impaired learning ability (Adachi et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2001; Ito-Ishida et al., 2015; Gemelli et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mecp2308/y and Viaat-Mecp2-/y mice almost recapitulate the entire spectrum of RTT features, including motor dysfunction, seizure, and stereotyped behaviors.
source: Furthermore, Mecp2308/y and Viaat-Mecp2-/y mice almost recapitulate the entire spectrum of RTT features, including motor dysfunction, seizure, and stereotyped behaviors (Chao et al., 2010; Shahbazian et al., 2002; Moretti et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mecp2308/y mice only display context-dependent fear memory deficits.
source: Interestingly, Mecp2308/y mice only display context-dependent fear memory deficits (Moretti et al., 2006); whereas, mice with PV-Mecp2-/y, CAMKII-Mecp2-/y, and MeCP2 region-specific deletions from the BLA only show cue-related fear memory deficits (Ito-Ishida et al., 2015; Adachi et al., 2009; Gemelli et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Mice with PV-Mecp2-/y, CAMKII-Mecp2-/y, and MeCP2 region-specific deletions from the BLA only show cue-related fear memory deficits.

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The amygdala has been emphasized as an essential component in the network that encodes fear.
source: The amygdala has been emphasized as an essential component in the network that encodes fear (Adolphs, 2013; Johansen et al., 2010; Maren and Quirk, 2004; Paton et al., 2006; Reijmers et al., 2007; Janak and Tye, 2015; Yu et al., 2017; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: NAc cholinergic interneurons are important to fear learning regardless of whether context or tone was tested.
source: Nevertheless, whether the NAc, a reward and aversion center in the brain, participates in fear has not been clearly ascertained (Floresco, 2015; Hu, 2016; Reynolds and Berridge, 2008; Russo and Nestler, 2013). Here, our evidence indicates that NAc cholinergic interneurons are important to fear learning regardless of whether context or tone was tested.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: NAc CIN receives converging input from both HPC and BLA.
source: The most probable explanation could be that NAc CIN receives converging input from both HPC and BLA, thus participating in both context and tone fear regulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by rabies tracing data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The function of BLA→NAc circuit has been well reported in tone fear.
source: In particular, the function of BLA→NAc circuit has been well reported in tone fear (Correia et al., 2016) and HPC→NAc circuit in contextual reward behavior (LeGates et al., 2018), indicating the involvement of NAc in both contextual and tone related behaviors.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The function of HPC→NAc circuit has been well reported in contextual reward behavior.
source: In particular, the function of BLA→NAc circuit has been well reported in tone fear (Correia et al., 2016) and HPC→NAc circuit in contextual reward behavior (LeGates et al., 2018), indicating the involvement of NAc in both contextual and tone related behaviors.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: NAc is a crucial brain region for emotional valence.
source: NAc is a crucial brain region for emotional valence (Hu, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Cholinergic interneurons of the NAc are tonic firing interneurons that provide rich local innervation to MSNs.
source: Cholinergic interneurons of the NAc are tonic firing interneurons that provide rich local innervation to MSNs (Higley et al., 2009), however, how they participate in fear learning is unclear.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: NAc cholinergic interneurons modulate their firing following exposure to cues associated with reward.
source: Accumulating evidence suggests that NAc cholinergic interneurons modulate their firing following exposure to cues associated with reward (Brown et al., 2012; Witten et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Reduced spontaneous activity of cholinergic interneurons can lead to depressive-like behaviors.
source: Furthermore, reduced spontaneous activity of cholinergic interneurons can lead to depressive-like behaviors (Cheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Blockade of GABAA receptors with bicuculline produces no obvious alteration in the firing rate of cholinergic interneurons.
source: Previous electrophysiological studies have suggested that blockade of GABAA receptors with bicuculline produces no obvious alteration in the firing rate of cholinergic interneurons (Bennett and Wilson, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Cholinergic interneurons only contribute about 2% of NAc neurons.
source: As cholinergic interneurons only contribute about 2% of NAc neurons (Kreitzer, 2009; Castro and Bruchas, 2019), scattered expression of α2-GABAA receptors in MSNs may buffer the difference resulting from cholinergic interneurons by western blot analysis (Mitchell et al., 2018; Koo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: MeCP2 is a transcriptional regulator that binds broadly throughout the genome and regulates the expression of thousands of genes.
source: MeCP2 is a transcriptional regulator that binds broadly throughout the genome and regulates the expression of thousands of genes (Chahrour et al., 2008; Cheng and Qiu, 2014; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Previous microarray analysis of gene expression profiles in Mecp2-null and Mecp2-Tg mice using hypothalamic RNA revealed dysregulation of the Gabra2 gene in those mouse models.
source: Previous microarray analysis of gene expression profiles in Mecp2-null and Mecp2-Tg mice using hypothalamic RNA revealed dysregulation of the Gabra2 gene in those mouse models (Chahrour and Zoghbi, 2007; Hogart et al., 2007; Samaco et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: α2-containing GABAA-receptor selective drugs do not induce tolerance.
source: As α2-containing GABAA-receptor selective drugs do not induce tolerance (Vinkers et al., 2012), they provide an attractive molecular target for treatment of fear-related neuropsychiatric disorders.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Modulation of the NAc may ameliorate fear-related disorders.
source: Taken together, these results reveal a previously unknown role of MeCP2 in NAc cholinergic interneurons in fear regulation, suggesting that modulation of neurons in the NAc may ameliorate fear-related disorders.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.
